statement: Let $u_{1}=1$ and $u_{n+1}=u_{n}+\frac{1}{u_{n}}$ for $n\ge 1$. (i) Find $u_{2},u_{3},u_{4}$. (ii) Prove by induction that $u_{n}^{2}\ge n$ for all $n\ge 1$. (iii) Deduce that $u_{n}\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$.
solution: (i) $u_{2}=1+1=2$, $u_{3}=2+\tfrac12=\tfrac52$, $u_{4}=\tfrac52+\tfrac25=\tfrac{29}{10}$. (ii) Base $u_{1}^{2}=1\ge 1$. Assume $u_{n}^{2}\ge n$. Then $u_{n+1}^{2}=(u_{n}+\tfrac1{u_{n}})^{2}=u_{n}^{2}+2+\tfrac1{u_{n}^{2}}\ge u_{n}^{2}+2\ge n+2\ge n+1$. (iii) From (ii), $u_{n}\ge \sqrt{n}\to\infty$, so the sequence diverges to infinity.
hints: Use the inductive hypothesis to bound u_{n+1}^2.
